body:
_Migrated from issue #1357, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate. A gap, not a broken claim — v4.1.29 only claims the
four routes that were fixed, and `test_1318_honest_commit_status.py`'s pinned list matches.

#1318 made rolled-back writes stop reporting success. `ub.session_commit()` now returns a
boolean for callers to check. `helper.edit_book_read_status` discards that boolean on **both**
branches, so these three still answer `200` unconditionally even when the write was rolled back:

- `POST /ajax/toggleread/<id>`
- `POST /api/v1/books/<id>/read`
- `POST /ajax/readselectedbooks`

Same class as the four already fixed (`set_bookmark`, `save_bookmark`, `delete_auth_token`,
`edit_domain`): the user is told their read status changed when it may not have.

Worth folding into the same contract rather than one-off patching — the pattern is now
established, and read status is a two-carrier write (#1343), so a half-failed toggle is exactly
where a silent success is most misleading.

Note on evidence: the refuter could not produce a clean live DB-busy repro, because an external
`BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` on `/config/app.db` blocked a third sqlite connection but did not block the
app (WAL over a Docker Desktop bind mount). So the un-checked return value is OBSERVED in
source; the runtime consequence is reasoned, not demonstrated.
title: Read-status toggle routes still report success on a rolled-back write (#1318 contract gap)
